clue.text: A horny, as well as a thorny, problem?

definitions.text: A horny, as well as a thorny, problem?

parts.words: A horny, as well as a thorny, problem?
parts.note: a hard choice is traditionally pictured as a bull with two horns, either of which may gore you, so the problem is both horned and prickly

explanation.walkthrough: One is said to be 'on the horns of' this kind of problem, which is why it is 'horny' as well as thorny.
explanation.definitionFit: A choice between two equally unwelcome options is classically described as having two horns.

clue.text: First-class student had up? What a bloomer!

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the whole run is read from bottom to top

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written here as AI
L is a learner, from the L-plate
taken as written

explanation.surface: A top student was fooled; what a blunder!
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a blunder but is a flowering plant; 'up' reverses AILHAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A showy garden flower is something that blooms.

clue.text: Piece of sugar is hard and heavy

parts.note: a lump of sugar is a sugar cube
taken as written
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A sugar cube is solid and weighty.
explanation.definitionFit: Clumsy and dull, like a lump.

clue.text: A custom he breaks, waxing it?

definitions.text: A custom he breaks, waxing it?

indicators.note: the words a custom he are broken apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: A man breaks with tradition by waxing something.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a man who waxes the hair on his upper lip breaks with custom.
explanation.definitionFit: Facial hair on the upper lip, which some men wax into points.

clue.text: Worsening annoyance

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from the verb meaning to exacerbate, and informally to irritate.

clue.text: It's supposed to be put on

definitions.meaning: adopted or feigned, as a false name or air is

explanation.surface: Something is meant to be worn.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share the past participle of a verb meaning to take on: a belief taken for granted, or a manner donned falsely.

clue.text: It's noted as material for Cockney's 3

definitions.meaning: a tune is written in musical notes
a Cockney drops the h, so the hair a 3-down is made of comes out without it

explanation.surface: Something documented as stuff for a Londoner's upper-lip growth.
explanation.walkthrough: 3 is 3-down, a growth of hair; a Cockney (a working-class Londoner) drops the H of 'hair'.
explanation.definitionFit: A melody is written in notes; and dropping the first letter of hair, as a Cockney does, leaves the word.

clue.text: In Euripides, a Tyrian wood-god

indicators.note: the deity is found sitting inside the run of words Euripides, a Tyrian

explanation.surface: A forest deity from Tyre appears in a play by Euripides.
explanation.walkthrough: Euripides did write a satyr play, the Cyclops, which makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: A goat-like woodland deity of Greek myth, companion of Dionysus.

clue.text: One may be inflamed by such a cocktail

definitions.text: One may be inflamed by such a cocktail

parts.words: One may be inflamed by such a cocktail
parts.note: the cocktail is not a drink but a petrol bomb, named after a Soviet minister, which sets things alight

explanation.walkthrough: 'inflamed' suggests drunken passion, but this cocktail is a bottle of petrol with a burning rag.
explanation.definitionFit: The name attached to the improvised petrol bomb, after the Soviet foreign minister.

clue.text: Energetic action disturbed Amy's mind

indicators.note: the letters of Amy's mind are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Some vigorous activity upset Amy.
explanation.definitionFit: Vigour and drive; forceful, active energy.

clue.text: Meat-cake (meat with egg on in British Rail)

parts.note: ham is a cured meat

indicators.note: the urging sits inside the railway initials

parts.note: BR is the abbreviation for British Rail, the former UK national railway
to egg someone on is to urge them

explanation.surface: A recipe note: a meat patty with ham and egg served on a train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egg on' looks like a topping but is the verb 'urge'; British Rail was the UK's state railway until the 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: A patty of minced beef is a kind of cake of meat, the old descriptive name for it.

clue.text: Claw the remaining cards

definitions.meaning: the hooked nail of a bird of prey
in card games, the undealt stock left after the deal

explanation.surface: An instruction to snatch whatever cards are left.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird of prey's hooked nail; also, in games like patience, the stock of undealt cards.

clue.text: A blinking one portrayed in the silver casket

definitions.text: A blinking one portrayed in the silver casket

parts.words: A blinking one portrayed in the silver casket
parts.note: in The Merchant of Venice, the Prince of Arragon opens the silver casket and finds a portrait of a blinking fool, a phrase that is also British slang

explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice the silver casket holds 'the portrait of a blinking idiot'; 'blinking' is also a mild British intensifier, as in 'blinking fool'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fool or simpleton, here the one pictured in Shakespeare's casket scene.

clue.text: This plantation a right bore to stomach!

parts.note: taken as written
tum is an informal word for stomach

explanation.surface: Someone finds a tree garden too dull to tolerate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to stomach' reads as 'to tolerate', but here 'stomach' is just the body part, placed after the bore.
explanation.definitionFit: A botanical collection planted with trees is a kind of plantation.

clue.text: Actions, in which French artist creates rackets

indicators.note: the artist goes inside the word for actions

parts.note: battles are military actions
Gustave Doré was a French illustrator

explanation.surface: Fights in which a French painter makes a din.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rackets' looks like noise, but means the bats used in the old game of shuttlecock.
explanation.definitionFit: Light bats used to hit a shuttlecock in an early form of badminton.

clue.text: So intimate that some criminals are stupid?

definitions.meaning: read literally, burglars who are dim-witted

explanation.surface: Two friends so close it is as if robbers were dim.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for close friendship; literally, robbers who are dense.

clue.text: In a tutelary spirit, say, it's skilfully contrived

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is spoken, giving a word that sounds like it

parts.note: a genius is a guardian spirit, so this is 'in genius'

explanation.surface: Being guided by a guardian spirit makes something clever.
explanation.walkthrough: A genius in Roman belief was a tutelary (guardian) spirit; 'in genius' spoken sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleverly devised; inventive and original.

clue.text: One deputed to watch proceedings weekly.

definitions.meaning: someone sent to monitor events, such as a delegate at talks
the British Sunday newspaper of that name

explanation.surface: A delegate keeps an eye on events every week.
explanation.definitionFit: A monitor sent to watch; and the name of a long-running British Sunday paper.

clue.text: One scientist accepts crate ordered for another

indicators.note: one scientist takes in another piece, so it acts as a container

parts.note: a biologist is a scientist who studies living things

indicators.note: the word crate is put into a new order

explanation.surface: A scientist takes delivery of a crate that has been ordered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' gives ACTER, which 'accepts' tucks in just after the scientist's first letter; the definition 'another' leans on 'One scientist' before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A germ specialist is another kind of scientist, following on from the first.

clue.text: Revolutionary means of beaching-for-instance

parts.note: a rotating drum that winds a rope, used to haul boats up a shore; revolutionary means it turns, not political

explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' sounds political, but this device revolves; it winds cables, for instance to haul a boat onto a beach.
explanation.definitionFit: A vertical rotating winch drum used to haul in ropes and cables.

clue.text: Additional identification of vessel in identical surroundings

indicators.note: the vessel goes in the middle of the identical word

parts.note: same means identical, here wrapped around the vessel
an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: A ship's extra label shows it in matching surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship but is a vase.
explanation.definitionFit: A family name added to a given name further identifies the person.

clue.text: Carefully examined 25 dn?

definitions.meaning: 25-down is a feline, and one taken to the animal doctor has been treated by him

explanation.surface: Has 25-down been thoroughly checked?
explanation.walkthrough: 25 dn is 25-down, a pet that would go to the animal doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Screened thoroughly; and literally treated at the animal doctor's.

clue.text: Made intelligible by former pressman of homely aspect

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
a plain face is a homely, unattractive one
ED is short for editor, a newspaper man

explanation.surface: An ex-newspaperman with an ordinary face made things clear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'former pressman' reads as one person, an ex-journalist, but the homely face goes between the two halves of that phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something clear and understandable is to account for it.

clue.text: We hear it said of the ear

indicators.note: we hear marks a word that sounds like another

parts.note: oral means spoken or said

explanation.surface: A remark about hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to hearing or the organ of hearing.

clue.text: Foster is a shark

definitions.meaning: to bring up or nurture a child
a ... shark is a species of shark

explanation.surface: A man called Foster turns out to be a swindler.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurture or rear; also a kind of shark of warm coastal waters.

clue.text: Curiously overt, Dame Christabel's campaign to be one

definitions.text: Dame Christabel's campaign to be one

indicators.note: the letters of overt are arranged in a curious, odd way

explanation.surface: Dame Christabel campaigned openly, oddly, to gain the ballot.
explanation.walkthrough: Dame Christabel Pankhurst was a leader of the British suffragettes, who campaigned for women to get the vote.
explanation.definitionFit: The suffragettes fought so that women could each cast a ballot in elections.

clue.text: Name in motor-car accident is Bird

indicators.note: the name letter goes in among the wrecked car letters
a car accident wrecks the word motor-car into a new order

explanation.surface: A driver called Bird is named in a car crash report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accident' rearranges MOTORCAR to CORMORAT, and 'in' places N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A large dark seabird that dives for fish.

clue.text: Spiteful woman-jazz enthusiast

definitions.meaning: old slang for a hep jazz fan

explanation.surface: A nasty woman who loves jazz.
explanation.definitionFit: A catty woman; and in 1940s jive slang, a cool jazz fan.

clue.text: Call to get permit? That depends on the head

parts.note: to ring someone is to telephone them
let means allow or permit

explanation.surface: Phoning for a permit, only to be told it depends on the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depends' is meant literally: it hangs down from the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A curl of hair hangs down from the scalp, so it literally depends from the head.

clue.text: Temporarily debar American writer in South Dakota

indicators.note: the American writer sits inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: SD is the postal abbreviation for South Dakota
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: An American author in South Dakota is banned for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: To bar from duty or membership for a limited time.
